title: The commit-msg hook's rule for naming an unclaimed item is findable in one message, so a release or planning commit needs no amends
goal: kbgit.py commit-msg tells, in its first refusal, which items a commit may name (claimed items of a started sprint, and for a planning commit only the items whose files it changes) and that a release commit of a released item names none; its text matches what sync's check-trailers gate then does with the same commit; found by the first supervised run (ST-opjydjc3): a runner's release commit took three amends, a planning commit one, and one commit was warned as refused yet pushed
notes: More evidence from the 2026-10-02..04 co-development feedback (mac-eighth's analysis): mac-third's first claim commit broke the trailer rules twice (BG-p4qdpbir); mac-fourth needed 3 amends on a runner release and 1 on a planning commit, and the commit-msg hook refused a KB-Work for an unclaimed item that the push gate then accepted; mac-sixth saw an amend re-run the hook and put a blank line before KB-Work (BG-5ykz2dte); mac-fifth needed amends for ST-xiyvkjro and BG-thez4izx planning commits.
